transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-11
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Khatri (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood CSM); Aisha Grant (Head of ML, Tidewater), Daniel Ruiz (SRE), Marta Ivanov (CTO), Ben Cho (Finance)

Summary (auto): Quarterly usage & reliability check. Discussed accelerating commitment for Dedicated, concerns on tail latency and KV cache persistence, and security/compliance gating. Agreed pricing + benchmark run and follow up.

00:00 Jordan: okay hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're running at 52 minutes today so we'll try to keep tight, um Jordan from Redwood here, i'm the account lead.
00:18 Aisha: hi yeah thanks, appreciate it, big week for us so i'll try to be concise.
00:25 Jordan: quick roll call - Priya from the se team, Samir is on for support and security handoffs.
00:32 Priya: hi all, nice to meet, i'm Priya - i'll be running the latency/cost benchmark with you.
00:40 Daniel: Daniel here, we'll be watching SLOs and infra impacts.
00:46 Marta: Marta, short on time but want to hear the contract options.
00:54 Ben: Ben in finance, want clarity on predictability.
01:02 Jordan: cool, first slide, usage trajectory - Aisha you shared growth is up ~3.4x qtr-over-qtr for inference calls? can you confirm?
01:18 Aisha: yeah that's right, active users doubled and the backend calls spiked, but it's uneven - we have big bursts around morning ET and some long tail chat sessions.
01:31 Priya: that distribution matters a lot for batching & autoscale, it will change unit costs. we saw your token profile, lots of short queries but some long context jobs.
01:46 Daniel: burstiness is our worry, we don't want queueing or p50/p95 to blow up during marketing spikes.
01:55 Jordan: got it. so we should walk through options: hosted with burst capacity vs Dedicated reserved pool. We also want to surface the degrade/fallback policy.
02:08 Aisha: our main criteria are p95 < 220ms for short prompts, cost under $0.0009 per token-equivalent, and audit logs for every request.
02:21 Priya: ok, p95 220ms is tight, depends on model family and sequence length; on-hosted you get best-effort low latency but no hard SLA unless we do a dedicated SL contract.
02:36 Jordan: correct. Dedicated gives you committed GPU pool and predictable tail latency; it also enables VPC options if you need it.
02:45 Marta: when you say "predictable" how do you model headroom? if we commit X, what happens on a 3x spike?
02:55 Jordan: two levers - reserved baseline + burst credits. you can configure autoscale thresholds; for big spikes we recommend burst capacity (pay-as-you-go top up) or a hybrid routing policy for critical routes.
03:10 Ben: finance question - if we buy Dedicated, do we get unit price guarantees versus hosted?
03:18 Jordan: yes, a blended committed rate; we present 3 tiers - 6m, 12m, 24m commitments with increasing discounts. i'll send the spreadsheet after the call.
03:28 Ben: okay please include breakpoints for usage bands so we can model.
03:33 Priya: action we'll include expected TCO comparisons using your burst profile.
03:40 Aisha: also security - we need KMS/HSM integration, SSO with SAML, and SOC2 Type II paperwork before any contract.
03:50 Samir: that's standard, we have a security packet. we'll need to map key rotation & KMS flow if you're doing private key management.
03:58 Marta: do you support customer-managed keys in the Private deployment?
04:04 Samir: yes, in Redwood Private you can bring your KMS, HSM and there's an air-gapped option. for Dedicated we can also do external KMS integrations in most cases.
04:16 Daniel: network wise we need to know IP allowlist, peering options and if logs can be forwarded to our SIEM.
04:24 Priya: we can export audit logs and request-level tracers, STS tokens are supported for temporary creds. we'll include the network diagram.
04:34 Jordan: okay on to latency numbers -- Priya, can you summarize the benchmark plan?
04:40 Priya: yes, plan is: run two 1-hour passes, one with your short prompt mix (90% < 64 tokens) and one with the blended real traffic. capture p50/p95/p99, cost per 1k tokens, token emission profiles and cold-start penalty. we'll run against hosted and then a Dedicated staging cluster sized as X GPUs.
04:58 Aisha: that sounds good, what about KV cache warm-up behavior? we've had cache thrash on other infra.
05:06 Priya: our runtime does continuous KV caching but you can pin session affinity to reduce thrash. one caveat: some transcriptions show "KV chash" or similar but it's a naming quirk in our internal logs, not a functional issue.
05:22 Daniel: will the benchmark test include long context sessions up to 16k?
05:27 Priya: yes we'll emulate your long-context jobs but might need to quantize model variant for cost; we'll note any quality delta.
05:36 Jordan: can we talk about rollback/fallback? if a model variant has regression we'll route to safe fallback model - that's part of rollout policies.
05:46 Aisha: good, we need guardrails on hallucination risk for help-center answers.
05:52 Priya: we'll include eval prompt sets and regression alert thresholds.
06:00 Ben: question on billing granularity - is it per-token, per-request, or both?
06:06 Jordan: primary is per-token but we also show per-request amortized cost and per-route breakdown in the Console. for Dedicated billing you get committed flat fee + overage; we'll show modeled invoices.
06:20 Marta: international data residency - some EU traffic needs to stay in eu-west, how is routing handled?
06:29 Samir: we support routing by region and model variant; we can pin routes to eu regions. Private deployment can stay on-prem if needed.
06:39 Aisha: curious, we heard another vendor offers cheaper rates but with higher latency; how does Redwood justify premium?
06:47 Jordan: two parts - predictable tail latencies and operational tooling (tracing, rollouts, cost per-token lineage). plus we optimize kernels + batching to lower real costs for production patterns.
06:59 Ben: okay finance will run comparison but we need a clear ROI case.
07:06 Priya: we'll produce a TCO page showing cost delta vs self-host and vs competitor at your traffic profile.
07:14 Aisha: anything about model updates? we want version pinning and ability to stage rollouts.
07:20 Jordan: yes model pinning, canary rollouts and automatic fallback. we'll demo the rollout UI if helpful.
07:28 Daniel: regarding SLAs, what uptime & latency SLAs do you offer for Dedicated?
07:34 Jordan: SLA tiers vary by commitment; standard is 99.9% uptime and latency SLO guarantees for critical routes in higher tiers. we'll attach the SLA language.
07:44 Marta: one more on compliance: can we get a copy of your SOC2 + pen test summary?
07:50 Samir: yes, sending security packet and pen test exec summary.
07:55 Jordan: ok let's capture next steps - Priya will own the benchmark scheduling.
08:00 Priya: noted. I'll reach out for SSH/ingest endpoints and credentials.
08:06 Aisha: we'll provide the prompt sets and traffic profile by Wednesday.
08:12 Ben: please include the financial cadence options and early-termination terms.
08:18 Jordan: agreed.
08:22 [crosstalk] Marta: can you also include escalation contacts?
08:28 Samir: yes, I'll include 24/7 oncall escalation path for Dedicated customers.
08:34 Jordan: any blockers we haven't covered?
08:38 Aisha: KMS flow diagrams and the benchmark window alignment with our maintenance blackout windows.
08:45 Priya: we'll coordinate for quiet windows.
08:49 Daniel: also need to validate our CI/canary integration for model rollouts, maybe a dry-run.
08:56 Priya: we can run a dry-run with limited traffic in the staging pool.
09:02 Jordan: last thing - pricing scenarios, we'll show one with a 12m commit and one with a 24m commit plus burst credits and one hybrid hosted + dedicated.
09:14 Ben: include break-even points and sensitivity to 2x/3x growth.
09:20 Jordan: great. quick recap of action items before we wrap.
09:25 Jordan: Priya schedule benchmark and request creds - due 2026-09-20.
09:29 Priya: yes.
09:31 Jordan: Samir send security packet + KMS notes - due 2026-09-13.
09:35 Samir: on it.
09:36 Jordan: Jordan to send pricing + committed scenarios - due 2026-09-15.
09:40 Jordan: Aisha to send prompt sets and traffic profile - due 2026-09-14.
09:44 Aisha: will do.
09:45 Marta: any open questions for me?
09:48 Marta: no, this is good.
09:51 Jordan: ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up in writing, expect the worksheet and security packet in the next 48 hours.
09:58 Ben: thanks all.
10:00 Meeting ends.
